proposals.before: On the homeward crossing of the Zhe the boat nearly capsized in a squall; Shami clung to the coffin and wailed, and soon the wind died—men took it as filial feeling answered from Heaven.

proposals.before: In Tianjian he began as court gentleman, rose to staff equal on the Prince of Jin'an of Xuanhui's staff with inner recorder duties, then magistrate of Xichang.
proposals.after: In Tianjian he began as court gentleman for attendance, rose to staff equal on the Xuanhui staff of the Prince of Jin'an with concurrent inner-recorder duties, then went out as magistrate of Xichang.
proposals.reason: Xuanhui is the general's title attached to the prince's staff, not a second princely title; the idiomatic phrase 'Prince of Jin'an of Xuanhui' reverses that structure.

proposals.before: In the Tianjian era he first entered office as court gentleman for attendance, then was promoted staff equal on the staff of the Prince of Xuanhui of Jin'an, concurrently inner recorder within limits, and went out to supplement magistrate of Xichang.
proposals.after: In the Tianjian era he first entered office as court gentleman for attendance, then was promoted staff equal on the Xuanhui staff of the Prince of Jin'an, concurrently inner recorder within limits, and went out to fill the post of magistrate of Xichang.
proposals.reason: The literal rendering 'Prince of Xuanhui of Jin'an' misreads 宣惠晉安王 as if Xuanhui were the princely title; 宣惠 modifies the staff, and 晉安王 is the prince.

proposals.before: When mourning for his father ended he wailed day and night, wasted away until only bone stood, and his mother Lady Ruan constantly watched over him herself to restrain and comfort him.

proposals.reason: 及丁父憂 marks the onset of mourning, not its end; 服闋後 in the next sentence is when mourning ended.

Literal “Prince of Xuanhui of Jin’an” misreads 宣惠 as the princely title; 宣惠 modifies the staff and 晉安王 is the prince. The proposed repair restores that order.
s0235 建康正 is the Jiankang rectifier; s0237’s later 建康令 shows magistrate is a distinct office, so “magistrate” here is wrong.

吾家陽元也 compares Xie Lan to the style-name Yangyuan (陽元), not a metaphysical “Yang element.”
Literal “Yang element” is the same mistranslation of the personal style 陽元; Yangyuan is required.
及丁父憂 marks entering mourning for his father; “when mourning ended” contradicts both 丁憂 and the following 服闋後 in s0263.
士林館，藺獻頌 separates the place from the subject Lan; without the comma, “Scholars' Grove Lan” fuses place and personal name and obscures who presented the eulogy.
